transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-11-01
- Time: 15:30 UTC
- Duration: ~47 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Lucas Chen (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (CTO, Peregrine), Diego Alvarez (ML Eng), Priyanka Singh (Product)

Summary:
Peregrine is evaluating Redwood for a short pilot to prove time-to-first-token (TTFT) for customer-facing summarization and a subsequent private deployment for PII-sensitive data. Main concerns are latency SLOs, encryption/KMS, and how free credits and pilot pricing map to a POC. They are leaning toward starting on hosted API for speed, with a gated path to Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem) if compliance sign-off requires it.

Topics: quickstart credits, TTFT, hosted vs dedicated vs private, SOC2/KMS/VPC, latency estimates, rollout strategy, success criteria, timeline

[00:00] Maya Thompson: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, im maya, im your AE. lucas is our se who will help with latency and architecture stuff.
[00:12] Aisha Rahman: hi thanks, ive got diego and priyanka with me. real quick, we want to validate ttft for our summarization microservice and figure out path to private.
[00:20] Lucas Chen: awesome. can you share current traffic shape? qps, typical token lengths?
[00:25] Diego Alvarez: yeah, right now prod-ish we see spikes to about 40 rps, average 12, and summaries average ~450 tokens inbound+out. very bursty midday, and tail latency matters for UX.
[00:40] Priyanka Singh: timeline is tight — we want a working prototype in 2–3 weeks to demo to ops and ciso.
[00:50] Maya Thompson: got it. so typical path we recommend is quickstart on hosted with free credits so you get to first token day 0–2, then move to a short reserved pilot with dedicated capacity if you need isolation, and then private (VPC) only if compliance requires it.
[01:05] Aisha Rahman: key question: what does 'time to first token' usually mean here? like from code to actual streaming token in prod?
[01:12] Lucas Chen: yeah rough breakdown — onboarding and SDK integration is minutes to an hour, then model selection and warm start (kv cache warm) can be minutes. for streaming token latency we expect median token latency in hosted at ~20–40ms on our curated small-llm, but it depends on model selection and batching. with your 450 token average, end-to-end latencies will be dominated by generation time.
[01:35] Diego Alvarez: 20–40ms per token is great but does that hold at 40 rps spikes?
[01:40] Lucas Chen: at spikes we use smart routing and autoscale; for bursts we recommend either reserved Dedicated pools or using our burst capacity config. there is still tradeoff: dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower p99 compared to heavily oversubscribed hosted.
[01:55] Aisha Rahman: our security team will ask about SOC 2, KMS, and audit logs. can you run through the private options?
[02:03] Maya Thompson: yes — we have SOC2 reports, SSO/SAML, and audit logging standard on Dedicated and Private. Private (VPC) gives you customer-managed network and optional on-prem package. KMS integrations available for encryption at rest, and we can support HSM in enterprise package. i'll share SOC2 and KMS docs after this call.
[02:20] Priyanka Singh: any gotchas with bringing models from our infra into your private offering? we want to bring some fine-tuned checkpoints.
[02:28] Lucas Chen: you can bring model artifacts. on private there are options: we support model pinning and rollouts. small friction with container formats and quantization — we usually recompile with our kernel selection. we will run a model onboarding check to surface incompatibilities.
[02:45] Diego Alvarez: ok — about cost, do the free credits cover enough for a realistic pilot? we need to run stress tests and end-to-end UX sims.
[02:53] Maya Thompson: we can provision $5k of credits for 30 days as a standard pilot offer; that typically covers integration, smoke tests, and a limited load test. if you need larger scale we can discuss a paid short-term reserved window.
[03:07] Aisha Rahman: what about data retention and logging on hosted? our compliance team will balk if logs retain PII.
[03:15] Lucas Chen: hosted by default retains logs for 30 days but you can opt out or configure retention. for PII we recommend Private or Dedicated with strict retention and customer-managed KMS. we also support disabling request logging per route.
[03:30] Priyanka Singh: can you show an example integration? how fast to get a PoC running?
[03:36] Maya Thompson: yes — typically devs use the SDK or REST, we have quickstart snippets. time to first token for simple calls can be under an hour from cloning the sample app.
[03:50] [screen share note: maya shares quickstart repo link: https://redwood.app/quickstarts/peregrine-summarize]
[04:05] Lucas Chen: for your throughput and 450 token average, i'd propose starting with a medium-sized model we host that balances latency and cost. we can also try a quantized variant to reduce cost and memory pressure.
[04:18] Diego Alvarez: are quantized models production-ready for us? we have hallucination sensitivity.
[04:24] Lucas Chen: quantization is good for cost but needs evaluation. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles per workload and run evals against your prompt sets so you can measure quality delta. we should run that in the pilot.
[04:40] Aisha Rahman: competitor question — we have an internal on-prem stack and also looked at Anthropic and OpenAI. what are the reasons to pick Redwood?
[04:48] Maya Thompson: our differentiator is production-first: predictable unit economics, routing and fallback, and the unified experience across hosted/dedicated/private. you get built-in rollouts and canary policies, and explicit tooling to optimize batching/caching which reduces per-token cost.
[05:05] Priyanka Singh: that sounds good. can you commit to an SLA for a pilot?
[05:10] Maya Thompson: for hosted quickstart pilots we don't usually offer a formal SLA, but for Dedicated pilots we can provide an uptime/latency target as part of the reserved agreement. for the pilot we'll agree on SLOs in the SOW.
[05:25] Diego Alvarez: i'd like Lucas to give a quick latency sketch based on our numbers — helps us set expectations for demo.
[05:30] Lucas Chen: sure — rough calc: 450 tokens * 25ms/token median = ~11.25s median generation for the chunk. add network and SDK overhead ~200–400ms. p99 will be higher; with Dedicated you compress p99. i'll run a more rigorous sim and share numbers.
[05:50] Aisha Rahman: ok. success criteria for us: 1) TTFT under 15s median for typical request, 2) integration in 2 weeks for product demo, 3) clear privacy path to VPC or private if CISO requires.
[06:05] Maya Thompson: perfect. i'll capture that and include in the SOW.
[06:12] Priyanka Singh: what about rollout after pilot — can we do canary or A/B with model variants?
[06:18] Lucas Chen: yes — Redwood supports canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback to compatible model variants if there is an incident. we also keep token-level cost metrics per route.
[06:30] Diego Alvarez: one more — are there standard connectors for our data stores? we use s3 and bigquery for user content index.
[06:38] Maya Thompson: we have connectors and sample ETL patterns — we'll link the docs. for private deployments we can also set up a transfer appliance if needed.
[06:50] Aisha Rahman: ok next steps from our side — we need the SOW and security docs, and diego will share a representative prompt set and small traffic trace for Lucas to run sims.
[07:00] Maya Thompson: great. i'll send SOW and SOC2/KMS/SAML docs. lucas will run sims after you share logs. we'll provision credits once we have internal approval.
[07:10] Priyanka Singh: timeline? we aim to run integration next week and have a demo with ops the following week.
[07:16] Maya Thompson: sounds doable. expected cadence: SOW by 11/3, sims by 11/5, credits provisioned upon NDA/approval.
[07:25] [brief cross-talk clarifications on invoicing and contact emails]
[07:40] Aisha Rahman: thanks everyone. appreciate the clear path.
[07:45] Maya Thompson: thanks all — follow-up in email with links to docs and SOW.
